title: Cite each block by a fixed label
statement: Give every block a short label that is never renumbered or reused, name every automatic finding by it, and show the labels beside any page that carries none.
detail: The lesson engine's composer gives each block a code and a number, keeps the highest number ever given per code, and never renumbers or reuses one (`g9/transformer/web/app.js`). Its playtest names every engine finding by the block's label (`g9/transformer/src/server.js`), and because the players' own pages carry no labels, a line over the frame names the blocks they are showing. The engine's own lesson view prints each label on the page (`g9/transformer/web/lesson.js`), and its decisions ask for a short identifier on every block to cite (`g9/transformer/DECISIONS.md`).

evidence.quote: the highest number ever given per code: numbers are never renumbered or reused
The composer shows the result as one line; an engine finding is named with its block's label
The block labels on the build's page now on screen, over the frame and on the strip (its pages carry none).
with a short identifier on every block (`QC-1`, `EH-2`) to cite
const tag = (id) => h("span", { class: "label brass", id: `tag-${id}` }, id);

The step is the page's own authored id, never its position: a position rots the moment the lesson changes shape, and it did — five probes pinned to `?page=<n>` moved to a different screen the day L1 grew an opening video.
